title: Greek Salad
subtitle: Classic horiatiki with tomatoes, feta, and olives
excerpt: A proper Greek salad has no lettuce. It is big chunks of ripe tomato and cucumber, good olives, plenty of oregano, and a block of feta sitting on top. Do not crumble the feta. This is one of those recipes that is only as good as its ingredients.
sourceNotes: Horiatiki, or village salad, is the Greek country salad that predates the tourist version served abroad. It uses whatever is ripe and available, dressed simply with olive oil and red wine vinegar, with a slab of feta placed on top rather than mixed through.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best assembled just before serving. The tomatoes and cucumber release water if left dressed for more than 20 minutes.

content.text: Cut everything into large pieces. This is a chunky salad and the pieces should be big enough to pick up with a fork. Small dice makes it look wrong and softens the vegetables too fast.

items.prepNote: cut into a thick slab or large crumble

content.text: Arrange the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, and olives on a large plate or shallow bowl.
Place the feta on top. Do not mix it in.
Whisk the olive oil and red wine vinegar together. Season with a little salt and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the whole salad.
Scatter the dried oregano over the feta and vegetables.
Serve immediately. Bring it to the table and let everyone break the feta as they serve themselves.

items.symptom: Salad is very watery on the plate.
items.cause: Dressed too far in advance or tomatoes were very ripe.
items.fix: Dress just before serving. Tilt the plate to pour off excess liquid.

items.cause: Feta varies widely in salt content between brands.
items.fix: Rinse the feta briefly in cold water before serving.

items.cause: Tomatoes not ripe enough or too little dressing.
items.fix: Use the ripest tomatoes available. Be generous with the oil.
